_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with Dupuytren's contracture with a palpable cord.

pivotal_trials.phase: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (adequate and well-controlled)
pivotal_trials.design: Up to three injections of Xiaflex 0.58 mg or placebo into a Dupuytren's cord at 4-week intervals, with a finger extension procedure if contracture persisted; all U.S. sites.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a fixed flexion deformity causing an MP or PIP joint contracture of at least 20 degrees in at least one finger other than the thumb.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving a reduction in contracture to 5 degrees or less by 30 days after the last injection.
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 64% CCH vs 7% placebo; difference 57% (95% CI 48%, 65%); p<0.001.

nct_ctgov.title: AA4500 (XIAFLEX™, Proposed Name) in the Treatment of Dupuytren's Contracture

pivotal_trials.phase: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (adequate and well-controlled)
pivotal_trials.design: Up to three injections of Xiaflex 0.58 mg or placebo into a Dupuytren's cord at 4-week intervals; all sites in Australia.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a fixed flexion deformity causing an MP or PIP joint contracture of at least 20 degrees in at least one finger other than the thumb.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving a reduction in contracture to 5 degrees or less by 30 days after the last injection.
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success 44% CCH vs 5% placebo; difference 39% (95% CI 18%, 56%); p<0.001.

key_safety: Based on the two pooled placebo-controlled Dupuytren's trials (Studies 1 and 2) through Day 90 (XIAFLEX N=249, placebo N=125), the most common adverse reactions (>=25%) were edema peripheral 73%, contusion 70%, injection site hemorrhage 38%, injection site reaction 35%, and pain in extremity 35%. Most serious: flexor tendon rupture occurred in 3 (0.3%) of 1082 patients treated with 0.58 mg; 11 (1.0%) patients had SAEs involving the injected extremity.
target_moa: Collagenases (AUX-I and AUX-II) hydrolyze collagen in its native triple-helical conformation, lysing collagen deposits; injection into a Dupuytren's cord (comprised mostly of collagen) causes enzymatic disruption of the cord.
modality: Enzyme — a fixed-ratio mixture of two purified microbial collagenases (AUX-I and AUX-II) isolated from fermentation of Clostridium histolyticum.

rems.type: A REMS was approved consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure benefits outweigh the risks of tendon rupture, serious injury to the injected extremity, and serious hypersensitivity reactions.

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee met September 16, 2009; voted on recommending approval: Yes=12, No=0, Abstain=0.

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of adult men with Peyronie's disease with palpable plaque and curvature deformity of at least 30 degrees

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for the treatment of adult men with Peyronie's disease with a palpable plaque and curvature deformity of at least 30 degrees and proposed modifications to the approved REMS.

description.text: Added dosing regimen of two concurrent injections into cords affecting multiple joints in same hand for adult Dupuytren's contracture patients

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application proposes to revise the prescribing information to include the following change in the dosing regimen: two concurrent injections of Xiaflex into palpable cords affecting multiple joints in the same hand in adult patients with Dupuytren's contracture with finger extension procedure 24 to 72 hours after injection; the risk of skin laceration requiring skin graft in patients treated with Xiaflex; and a proposed modification to the approved REMS.

description.text: Added information on recurrence rate, safety/efficacy of retreatment of recurrent Dupuytren's contractures, and immunogenicity after retreatment

citations.quote:
- Supplement 85 proposes the addition of information related to the rate of recurrence of Dupuytren's contracture after a Xiaflex injection.
- Supplement 87 proposes the addition of information related to the safety and efficacy of retreatment of recurrent contractures.
- Supplement 88 proposes additional immunogenicity data after retreatment of recurrence and five years after initial Xiaflex treatment.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation granted for the treatment of (advanced) Dupuytren's Disease.

citations.quote: The Agency has granted Xiaflex an orphan designation for the treatment of advanced Dupuytren's Disease.
Because collagenase clostridium histolyticum has an orphan drug designation for this indication, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: BLA 125338 for Xiaflex (collagenase clostridium histolyticum) was received February 27, 2009 and approved February 2, 2010 as the first non-surgical treatment for adult Dupuytren's contracture with a palpable cord. It carried orphan drug designation for Dupuytren's Disease (exempting it from PREA pediatric requirements) and was approved with a REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) plus a 505(o) postmarketing requirement and numerous CMC/immunogenicity commitments. The Arthritis Advisory Committee voted 12-0 in favor of approval.

citations.quote: Please refer to your biologics license application (BLA), dated and received February 27, 2009, submitted under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act (PHSA) for Xiaflex (clostridial collagenase histolyticum).
We have approved your biologics license application for clostridial collagenase histolyticum effective this date, February 2, 2010.
The Agency has granted Xiaflex an orphan designation for the treatment of advanced Dupuytren's Disease.

Your proposed REMS, submitted on February 2, 2010, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

requirement.text: Submit an in vitro study of human sera from patients who received multiple Xiaflex injections to evaluate cross-reactivity of anti-product antibodies (anti-AUX-I and anti-AUX-II) with endogenous human MMPs (MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, MMP-8, and MMP-13).

citations.quote: Submit an in vitro study of human sera from patients who have received multiple Xiaflex injections to evaluate the potential for cross-reactivity of anti-product antibodies (i.e., anti-AUX-I and anti-AUX-II) with endogenous human MMPs (including MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, MMP-8, and MMP-13) with similar homology and relevance to the protein components of Xiaflex.
